capitals.note: Lead: "Their capitals included Yayatinagara (modern Binka) and Abhinava-Yayatinagara (modern Jajpur)"; Kataka "identified as Chaudwar near modern Cuttack" in Janmejaya I's 31st year. The dates of the moves are not given; coordinates approximate.

capitals.name: Abhinava-Yayatinagara (Jajpur)
capitals.note: Second capital named in the lead (infobox: "Abhinava-Yayatinagara (modern Jajpur)"); "The capital was later moved to the Bhauma-Kara capital Guheshvarapataka (modern Jajpur)". The Jajpur page (opened 2026-10-19) says only that "the later Somavanshi kings moved their capital from Yayatinagara (modern Binka) to Guheshvarapataka" and gives no date; 1101 stays a placeholder, to be bridged by the reader (Karnadeva c. 1100-1110).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Somavamshi row). Review fix 2026-10-19: Kosala only. The former shape added a 70 km disc at Cuttack (Kataka), 69 cells that bhauma-kara-dynasty draws until 950; the Somavamshi page says only that Janmejaya I (c. 882-922) "probably controlled a part of coastal Odisha" and that three grants of his 31st regnal year were issued from Kataka ("Chaudwar near modern Cuttack"), which "suggests that his influence extended to eastern Odisha by the end of his reign". That is influence, not annexation, and Bhauma-Kara rulers are still listed to the 10th century, so the coast is not drawn until the next keyframe. The Panduvamshi predecessors were in Dakshina Kosala; the page gives no area and says "It is not clear when the Somavamshis gained control over most of Odisha". The 100 km Sambalpur disc is drawn without the 13 cells that fall inside the Bhauma-Kara disc (bhauma-kara-dynasty, 170 km round Bhubaneswar), so the two dossiers do not draw the same land before 950; the capital Binka lies outside that disc.

correction.text: Kosala and the former Bhauma-Kara territories of coastal Odisha

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review fix 2026-10-19). "By the time of Dharmaratha [c. 980-1005], the Somavamshis had taken control of the former Bhauma-Kara territories" (page); the page does not date the takeover ("it is not known how exactly this happened") and Janmejaya I's daughter ruled the Bhauma-Kara throne as Tribhuvana-Devi II from around 894, a dynastic link. 950 is the bridge year that bhauma-kara-dynasty uses for its loss and dissolve, so the two ledgers are matched on it. The coast is that dossier's 170 km disc round Bhubaneswar without the Brahmapur and Rayagada discs (southern Odisha, Kalinga proper, drawn by eastern-ganga-kingdom): the part of the Bhauma-Kara disc that reaches Ganjam is not claimed by the Somavamshi page.

correction.text: as the previous shape without Dakshina Kosala around Bilaspur, conquered by Kalinga-raja

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review fix 2026-10-19). "Kalinga-raja conquered the Dakshina Kosala region from the Somavamshi dynasty" (Ratnapura page: "around 1000 CE"); the Somavamshi page: "The Kalachuris of Ratnapura conquered some western parts of the Somavamshis". Only the 120 km Bilaspur disc of kalachuris-of-ratnapura is taken off (4 cells of the Sambalpur disc); neither page gives a boundary. Not drawn: the loss of Kosala and Utkala "to rival chiefs" that the page implies before Yayati II (c. 1021), which it does not date.

correction.text: Kosala and Utkala (western, northern and coastal Odisha); southern Odisha (Kalinga) is not drawn

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; review fix 2026-10-19: was all of Odisha (568 cells). Under Yayati II the dynasty "re-established the Somavamshi control over Kosala and Utkala, which had been lost to rival chiefs". "One of his inscriptions describes him as the lord of Kalinga, Kosala, and Utkala" (inscription not named, undated): that is a title, not a statement of control, so Kalinga is not drawn. The Kalinga land is the Brahmapur (110 km) and Rayagada (80 km) discs that eastern-ganga-kingdom draws as Kalinga proper in 1056-1117 (117 of its cells lay in the former shape). Ratnapura's Dakshina Kosala is excluded. The page also says the last king Karnadeva's kingdom "was confined to the coastal tract between the present-day Balasore and Puri districts" (c. 1100-1110) and that the dynasty "lost its territories to the Nagas in the north-west, and the Gangas in the south": undated, so not drawn here (see the notes).

ledger.note: c. 882: Janmejaya I rules in Kosala. The table gives his reign as "c. 882-922"; the page does not explicitly name a founder or founding date and the infobox says "c. 9th century CE"; the infobox predecessors are the Bhauma-Kara dynasty and the Panduvamshis of Dakshina Kosala, and the Kalachuris of Tripuri drove the Panduvamshis from Kosala (undated). Review fix 2026-10-19: Cuttack removed from the founding region, see the 950 gain.

"By the time of Dharmaratha, the Somavamshis had taken control of the former Bhauma-Kara territories"; "it is not known how exactly this happened". The year matches bhauma-kara-dynasty's loss and dissolve, which use 950 for "the 10th century"; the page's own bound is Dharmaratha (c. 980-1005). The region is that dossier's disc without the Ganjam fringe.

ledger.note: c. 1000: Kalinga-raja conquers Dakshina Kosala. "Kalinga-raja conquered the Dakshina Kosala region from the Somavamshi dynasty" (Ratnapura page, "around 1000 CE"); the Somavamshi page says "conquered some western parts of the Somavamshis" without a year. The region is the overlap of the two dossiers' shapes (4 cells); matches kalachuris-of-ratnapura /ledger/0.

region.text: Kosala and Utkala beyond the previous shape, re-established from rival chiefs

ledger.note: c. 1021 (bridge): Yayati II restores Kosala and Utkala. He "re-established the Somavamshi control over Kosala and Utkala, which had been lost to rival chiefs"; the table dates his reign "c. 1021-1040". Review fix 2026-10-19: the region is the part of the new shape outside the previous one (the earlier shapes already hold Kosala and the Bhauma-Kara coast); the page implies Kosala and Utkala had been "lost to rival chiefs" before Yayati II without dating the loss, which is not drawn.
1021: a Chola army raids the Somavamshi capital. The page mentions "the 1021 Chola invasion of their capital Yayatinagara"; it does not name Rajendra or a route.
1021: the page gives the raid only, no occupation or withdrawal.
by 1114: Anantavarman Chodaganga ends the Somavamshis. "By 1114, the Somavamshi king had fallen to the Ganga king Anantavarman Chodaganga." The page does not give 1112 or 1118.
by 1114: the Somavamshi rule ends. Lead: "The Somavamshi rule ended in the early 12th century"; infobox "Disestablished: c. 12th century CE".

Review 2026-10-19: Anantavarman Chodaganga page: "the Sindurapura grant issued in the saka year 1040 (1118 A.D)" gives him sovereignty "over entire of the whole Utkala" and Madalapanji "defeated the last Kesari king Mahasivagupta" (= Karnadeva in the Somavamshi table); the Somavamshi page's "By 1114" is kept for the end of the dynasty. The zone is the corrected Kosala-and-Utkala shape.

notes: Cliopatria has no Somavamshi row. The page does not name a founder or founding date, so 882 is the first table reign; the Chola raid year is the page's. 'Panduvamshi dynasty' (Dakshina Kosala) and 'Shailodbhava' need a gap-filler; the Kalachuris of Ratnapura took western parts (undated). The 1114 end is 'by 1114' - Anantavarman Chodaganga's conquest year (1112/1118 in other accounts) is not on the page. Review fixes 2026-10-19: (1) Kosala only in 882-949; the coast (the Bhauma-Kara country) is a gain of 950 from bhauma-kara-dynasty, matching its loss and dissolve; the Cuttack disc is gone from 882-949, so the 69 cells drawn twice are resolved. The page's own bound for the takeover is 'By the time of Dharmaratha' (c. 980-1005); Janmejaya I's Kataka grants (c. 912) show influence only. (2) 1021-1113 is Kosala and Utkala without southern Odisha (Brahmapur and Rayagada discs, the land eastern-ganga-kingdom draws as Kalinga proper): 451 of the former 568 cells remain before the Bilaspur cut, none of them in eastern-ganga-kingdom's 1056 and 1102 shapes. The Kalinga title of Yayati II is not drawn. (3) New loss c. 1000 of Dakshina Kosala around Bilaspur to kalachuris-of-ratnapura (confidence 2, 4 cells), from the Ratnapura page. (4) 1114 versus 1118: the Somavamshi page says 'By 1114'; the Anantavarman Chodaganga page gives only the Sindurapura grant of 1118 claiming the whole of Utkala and names the last king Mahasivagupta (the Somavamshi table's regnal name for Karnadeva); the end stays 1114 and eastern-ganga-kingdom's 1118 gain from 'Somavamshi dynasty' (free text) should become a gain from somavamshi-dynasty at 1114 or note the gap. (5) The Jajpur page gives no date for the capital move; 1101 stays a placeholder. Not drawn (undated on the page, left to a gap-filler): Karnadeva's kingdom 'confined to the coastal tract between the present-day Balasore and Puri districts' and the losses 'to the Nagas in the north-west, and the Gangas in the south'; the loss of Kosala and Utkala 'to rival chiefs' before Yayati II. The 1021 Chola raid (Yayatinagara) is still missing from chola-empire.
